Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

disceptātiō

disceptātiō, disceptātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a debate, the arguing out of a disputed point

In this lexicon

  • debate

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.34: ūnum per disceptātiōnem, alterum per vim; Traupman 179, 301

Examples

  • nam cum sint duo genera dēcertandī, ūnum per disceptātiōnem, alterum per vim, cumque illud proprium sit hominis, hoc bēluārum, cōnfugiendum est ad posterius, sī ūtī nōn licet superiōre

    for there are two ways of settling a dispute, one by debate and the other by force, and since the first belongs to man and the second to beasts, we may resort to the second only if we cannot use the firstCic. Off. 1.34
